taxonomy.subtopic: Misfolded immunoglobulin light chains and Congo-red-positive fibrils

questions.stem_html:
A 66-year-old man has progressive edema, orthostatic lightheadedness, numb feet, and exertional dyspnea. Urine protein excretion is 5.8 g/day. Echocardiography shows thick ventricular walls with low-voltage electrocardiographic complexes. Serum immunofixation identifies a monoclonal lambda light chain. Abdominal fat-pad biopsy contains Congo-red-positive material with apple-green birefringence.

Which protein is the principal precursor of the deposited fibrils?

options.text_html: Serum amyloid A generated during chronic inflammation
Monoclonal immunoglobulin light chains produced by a plasma-cell clone
Beta-2 microglobulin retained during long-term dialysis
Calcitonin produced by thyroid parafollicular cells

questions.explanation_html: Misfolded monoclonal light chains aggregate into beta-pleated-sheet fibrils. Multiorgan AL amyloidosis commonly involves kidneys, heart, peripheral/autonomic nerves, and soft tissues. The monoclonal lambda protein directly identifies an immunoglobulin light-chain precursor, making this systemic AL amyloidosis.

wrong_choice_explanations.1: Serum amyloid A forms AA amyloid and would fit longstanding inflammatory disease rather than a monoclonal light-chain process.
wrong_choice_explanations.2: Transthyretin amyloid can cause cardiomyopathy and neuropathy, but a monoclonal light chain and nephrotic proteinuria point to AL amyloid.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Dialysis-related amyloid primarily affects osteoarticular structures in patients with prolonged renal replacement therapy.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Calcitonin-derived amyloid is localized to medullary thyroid carcinoma.

questions.educational_objective: Differentiate AL amyloidosis from AA, transthyretin, dialysis-related, and localized amyloid by linking the clinical context to the fibril precursor.
